question: How does Redis Pub/Sub work and when should you use it vs a message queue?
title: Redis Pub/Sub vs Message Queues
direct_answer: Redis Pub/Sub: publish a message to a channel, all current subscribers receive it. No persistence — if no subscriber is listening, the message is lost. No retry on failure. Use for real-time notifications, live dashboard updates, websocket fan-out. Use a message queue (Celery + Redis/RabbitMQ, Kafka) when you need: delivery guarantees, retry on failure, message persistence, consumer groups, or exactly-once processing.
interviewer_intent: Tests Redis feature depth and ability to choose the right messaging tool.

sections.title: Redis Pub/Sub in Python
sections.content:
import redis.asyncio as aioredis
import asyncio

r = aioredis.from_url('redis://localhost')

# Publisher — send notification
async def publish_user_update(user_id: int, event: dict) -> None:
    await r.publish(f'user:{user_id}:updates', json.dumps(event))

# Subscriber — WebSocket handler
async def subscribe_to_user_updates(user_id: int, websocket):
    pubsub = r.pubsub()
    await pubsub.subscribe(f'user:{user_id}:updates')
    try:
        async for message in pubsub.listen():
            if message['type'] == 'message':
                await websocket.send_text(message['data'])
    finally:
        await pubsub.unsubscribe()

# Pattern subscribe
async def subscribe_all_events(websocket):
    pubsub = r.pubsub()
    await pubsub.psubscribe('user:*:updates')  # wildcard pattern
    async for message in pubsub.listen():
        if message['type'] == 'pmessage':
            await websocket.send_text(message['data'])

seo.metaDescription: Redis Pub/Sub: publish to channels, async subscriber pattern, WebSocket fan-out, and when to use message queues instead.

speakable_v2.hook: Redis Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget — if no subscriber is listening when you publish, the message is gone.

beats.content: Pub/Sub is for real-time broadcast: live notifications, WebSocket fan-out, dashboard updates. Publish to a channel, all current subscribers get it. No persistence, no retry.
If any of these matter: delivery guarantee, retry on failure, message persistence, consumer groups — use a message queue. Redis Streams, Celery, Kafka all provide these. Pub/Sub doesn't.

speakable_v2.cap: Redis Streams is the persistent alternative to Pub/Sub — messages survive subscriber crashes and can be replayed. Use Streams when messages must not be lost.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Redis Streams for persistent messaging, or keyspace notifications for cache invalidation triggers.
